as_told.title: ScanPyramids muon scanning funded by a Japanese team with the Ministry of Antiquities

plain: The story is about a scientific effort called ScanPyramids, begun in 2015, that looks inside the Giza pyramids using muons. Muons are tiny particles that rain down from space and pass through stone, so measuring how many get through can reveal hidden empty spaces. Filippo Biondi, a scientist who has run his own radar scans beneath the pyramids, describes the project to Michels: it 'is using muons which are sub particles that are emitted from the universe.' The researcher Jeffrey Drum, who argues the pyramids were energy machines, adds who is behind it. He says a Japanese team 'has been sponsoring and providing the funding for all of this,' working with Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, and he points to the team's paper on its muon results. Both bring it up as an established mainstream project whose finds of hidden voids give a backdrop to their own, bolder claims about what lies inside and under the pyramids.
